content.overview: Section 47 sets out voting rights on poll: every member of a company limited by shares holding equity shares has a right to vote on every resolution, with voting power proportional to paid-up equity capital. Preference shareholders generally vote only on resolutions that affect rights attached to preference shares, winding-up, or reduction of share capital, with specified exceptions when dividends are in arrears.
content.glance: Equity holders vote on every resolution proportionate to paid-up equity; preference holders vote mainly on rights-affecting, winding-up and capital-reduction resolutions; arrears of dividend can enlarge preference voting.
content.study: Subject to section 43 and section 50(2), every member of a company limited by shares and holding any equity share capital has a right to vote on every resolution placed before the company, and voting right on a poll is in proportion to the paid-up equity share capital. Preference shareholders have a right to vote only on resolutions which directly affect the rights attached to their preference shares, and on any resolution for winding up or for repayment or reduction of share capital. Where the dividend on preference shares is in arrears for a prescribed period, preference shareholders may acquire voting rights on all resolutions as provided. Current-law framing: identify class of shares; apply equity voting or limited preference voting; check dividend arrears for expanded preference rights.

sections.heading: Equity Voting
sections.body: Equity shareholders vote on every resolution; on a poll, votes are proportional to paid-up equity capital.

sections.heading: Preference Voting — Limited
sections.body: Preference shareholders vote on resolutions that directly affect preference rights, and on winding-up or reduction/repayment of capital.

sections.heading: Preference Voting — Expanded
sections.body: Where preference dividends are in arrears for the prescribed period, preference shareholders may vote on all resolutions as provided.

examples.title: Equity poll
examples.body: On a poll, an equity holder with twice the paid-up equity capital of another has twice the voting power under s. 47.

examples.title: Preference on rights variation
examples.body: A resolution altering preference dividend rights triggers preference shareholders’ right to vote under s. 47.

hypotheticals.question: Can preference shareholders vote on an ordinary business resolution when dividends are current?
hypotheticals.analysis: Generally no, unless the resolution directly affects preference rights or is for winding-up or capital reduction/repayment. Arrears of dividend can expand voting.

distinctions.title: Voting rights (s. 47) vs kinds of share capital (s. 43)
distinctions.left: Who may vote and on what

misconceptions.trap: Preference shareholders always vote on every resolution.
misconceptions.correction: Preference voting is generally limited to rights-affecting, winding-up and capital-reduction resolutions, subject to arrears expansion.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 47 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify class of shares. II. Apply equity or preference voting rules. III. Check dividend arrears. IV. Conclude on voting rights.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Share class; resolution type; arrears status; voting entitlement; precise relief.
